source: Six learning exchanges saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Readiness agreement, not yet and ready now
summary: Correctly matched listo/lista in five consecutive immediate practice contexts, including a double-negative reason sentence. Introduced todavía no and ya. Correctly used ya in a feature-readiness statement, then chose the valid sentence-final position in Podemos usarla ya. Accents and Spanish spelling of función remained supplied.

observations.outcome: Correct masculine agreement, readiness verb and negation placement. Standard capitalization and accent supplied.
Correct feminine agreement and affirmative meaning. Supplied Spanish función and the accent in está.

observations.learnerText: No podemos usarla porque No esta lista
observations.correctedText: No podemos usarla porque no está lista.
observations.outcome: Correct two negatives, feminine object la, unstated subject in the reason clause and feminine lista. Standard spelling supplied. Tutor then introduced todavía no with a readiness model.

observations.learnerText: El Logo todavia No esta listo
observations.correctedText: El logo todavía no está listo.
observations.outcome: Correct todavía no placement and masculine agreement after a feminine model. Supplied accents/capitalization. Tutor then introduced ya for ready now.
Correct ya and feminine agreement after a masculine model. Spanish función and accent supplied.

Correct use of sentence-final ya and feminine object la without being given the full target form. Tutor confirmed Ya podemos usarla is also natural. This is immediate transfer; no long-gap retention test.

nextSteps: Turn the valid can-use-it-now statement into a yes/no question
Recheck readiness gender with new familiar nouns after a gap
Preserve polarity and distinguish not yet from ready now
Treat ongoing accent/función spelling separately from correct grammar
assessmentNote: Agreement was consistent in this immediate round after earlier corrections. Long-term retention is unassessed; standard spelling was still supplied.
